answer: To resist Sybil attacks, implement Stake-Bonded TPM Attestation. First, each agent must lock $10,000 in crypto-bonds. Second, the local hardware TPM generates a unique, non-replicable cryptographic identity signature. Third, the network validates this signature against a quartz-hardened registry of verified hardware. Fourth, only these verified agents earn rewards. An attacker faces a cost of $100,000 in bonds and 30 days of hardware sourcing. This process ensures that a fraudulent agent is merely a fading ember, unable to disrupt the intricate sonnet of the consensus layer.
